sections.markdown:
## C — Sharing the road part one: required stops, school bus lights and penalties, school patrols and flaggers, right-of-way and yielding, emergency vehicles and the Move Over Law, careless and reckless driving, traffic stops, fleeing, pedestrians, crosswalks and bicyclists
Knowledge domain: when Minnesota law requires a full stop, how to behave around school buses, safety patrols and emergency vehicles, who yields to whom, what to do when an officer pulls you over, and how to share the road with pedestrians and bicyclists.

FACT_ID: sec07-F01 | anchor: A01
At a stop sign you must stop completely, before the stop line if one is marked, or before the crosswalk if there is one. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec07-F02 | anchor: A01
After stopping at a stop sign, yield to pedestrians, bicyclists and traffic before you go, and if your view of the intersection is blocked, be ready to stop again. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec07-F03 | anchor: A01
Stop completely before pulling onto a road from an alley, a private driveway, a parking lot or a parking ramp, and always stop before driving across a sidewalk or crosswalk. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec07-F04 | anchor: A01
At a red traffic signal, stop and wait until the light is green and your path is clear before going. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec07-F05 | anchor: A01
Stop at any crosswalk, marked or unmarked, where a pedestrian or bicyclist is crossing, and stay stopped until they have passed your lane. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec07-F06 | anchor: A01
Treat a flashing red traffic light exactly like a stop sign. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec07-F07 | anchor: A01
Full stops are also required for a red freeway ramp meter, for a railroad crossing posted with a stop sign, when a flag person or traffic device signals you to halt, and at a bridge raised for boats. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec07-F08 | anchor: A01
In a speed zone of 35 mph or less, a school bus driver turns on the flashing yellow lights at least 100 feet before the bus stops. [A01]
Why it matters: the two school bus warning distances are easy to swap.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec07-F09 | anchor: A01
In a speed zone above 35 mph, a school bus driver turns on the flashing yellow lights at least 300 feet before the bus stops. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec07-F10 | anchor: A01
Passing a school bus on its right side while it shows flashing red or yellow lights is against the law. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec07-F11 | anchor: A02
When a stopped school bus has its red lights flashing, you must stop at least 20 feet away from it. [A02]
Why it matters: the school bus stopping distance is one of the most tested numbers in the manual.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec07-F12 | anchor: A02
Whether you are facing the front or the back of the bus, you stay stopped until its red lights stop flashing. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec07-F13 | anchor: A02
Failing to stop for a school bus is a misdemeanor, and a conviction brings a fine of at least $500 and the loss of your driving privileges. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec07-F14 | anchor: A02
On a divided roadway you do not have to stop for a school bus with flashing red lights that is on the other side of the divider. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec07-F15 | anchor: A03
The owner or lessee of a vehicle used to break the school bus stopping law is guilty of a petty misdemeanor unless they can prove someone else was driving, in which case the driver is charged. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec07-F16 | anchor: A03
Come to a complete stop for a student safety patrol helping classmates cross, and for an adult crossing guard holding a stop sign or flag. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec07-F17 | anchor: A03
Driving through a line of children crossing the road is illegal even with no safety patrol present; it is a misdemeanor, and a second violation within a year is a gross misdemeanor. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec07-F18 | anchor: A03
Stop for a school bus flagger who is holding traffic so buses can leave school property, and do not move on until the flagger or a police officer tells you to. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec07-F19 | anchor: A03
At an intersection without signals, and at an all-way stop or flashing red light, when two drivers arrive together the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right. [A03]
Why it matters: left yields to right is a classic right-of-way item.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec07-F20 | anchor: A03
When turning left, yield to oncoming vehicles that are in the intersection or near enough to cause a crash. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec07-F21 | anchor: A03
A green left-turn arrow still requires you to yield to vehicles or pedestrians already in the intersection before you continue in the arrow's direction. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec07-F22 | anchor: A03
At an uncontrolled T intersection, the driver who is turning yields to all cross traffic. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec07-F23 | anchor: A03
A driver in the right-hand lane yields to transit and metro mobility buses merging out of a bus stop or off the shoulder, and to a school bus re-entering the lane after loading, which shows its left turn signal. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec07-F24 | anchor: A03
Yield to every vehicle in a funeral procession once it marks itself with headlights or hazard warning lights. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec07-F25 | anchor: A04
When an emergency vehicle with flashing red lights and a siren or bell comes toward you on a two-way road, move right and stop; on a one-way road move to the closer side; finish crossing an intersection first if you are in one; and stay stopped until every emergency vehicle has gone by. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec07-F26 | anchor: A04
You need not stop for an emergency vehicle that is separated from your lane by a physical barrier such as a fence, wall or median strip. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec07-F27 | anchor: A04
Under the Move Over Law, when an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is stopped on or beside a road with two lanes in your direction, move to the lane farthest from it if it is safe; tow trucks count as emergency vehicles. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec07-F28 | anchor: A04
If you cannot move over a lane, or the road has only one lane in your direction, slow down and pass the stopped vehicle with caution. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec07-F29 | anchor: A04
Only vehicles on official emergency business may follow within 500 feet of a firefighting vehicle on an emergency run. [A04]
Why it matters: the fire vehicle following distance is a likely numeric item.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec07-F30 | anchor: A04
Careless driving endangers people or property, while reckless driving means knowingly ignoring a substantial and unjustifiable risk to others, which includes racing whether or not the speed limit is exceeded. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec07-F31 | anchor: A05
When emergency lights appear behind you, stay calm, slow down, signal and pull onto the right shoulder as soon as it is safe, avoiding bridges, curves and the traffic lane. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec07-F32 | anchor: A05
During a stop after dark, switch on the interior light, keep the doors shut, stay inside unless the officer says otherwise, and keep your hands visible on the steering wheel. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec07-F33 | anchor: A05
With a firearm in the vehicle, leave both hands visible on the wheel, tell the officer about the firearm and its location as soon as they approach, and never reach for it. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec07-F34 | anchor: A06
Accepting a citation is not an admission of guilt; it only acknowledges that you received it and promises that you will appear in court if required. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec07-F35 | anchor: A06
Fleeing a police officer in a motor vehicle is a felony punishable by up to three years and one day in prison, a fine of up to $5,000, or both. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec07-F36 | anchor: A07
Passing a vehicle that has stopped for a pedestrian is illegal, so when another vehicle stops, look for someone in the crosswalk and be ready to stop. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec07-F37 | anchor: A07
Watch for blind pedestrians carrying a white or metallic cane or using a guide dog, and do not honk or rev the engine near them. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec07-F38 | anchor: A07
A marked crosswalk has solid white lines and may have signs or flashing lights, while an unmarked crosswalk is where a sidewalk meets the road with no lines painted. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec07-F39 | anchor: A07
Bicycles are legal vehicles on Minnesota roads with the same rights and responsibilities as other vehicles. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec07-F40 | anchor: A08
Driving in a bicycle lane is illegal except to park where allowed, to enter or leave the road, or to prepare for a turn, and you must yield to approaching bicyclists before moving into it. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec07-F41 | anchor: A08
When passing a bicyclist, leave at least 3 feet between the side of your car and the rider. [A08]
Why it matters: the bicycle passing clearance is a likely numeric item.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec07-F42 | anchor: A08
When it is safe, you may cross the center of the road to pass a bicyclist even in a no passing zone, after making sure the rider is not signaling or turning left. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec07-F43 | anchor: A08
Bicyclists must obey all traffic laws, ride with the flow of traffic, signal every turn and obey traffic control signs, signals and devices. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec07-F44 | anchor: A08
At a stop sign a bicyclist must slow enough to be able to stop before the intersection or crosswalk, and may continue without stopping when no vehicle is nearby. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0051]

Misconceptions: you must stop for a school bus with red lights flashing whether you are behind it or facing it, unless a divider separates you on a divided road; a green arrow does not cancel the duty to yield to people already in the intersection; accepting a ticket is not admitting guilt; a no passing zone does not forbid safely crossing the center to pass a bicyclist.
Mnemonics: yellow one hundred in slow zones, three hundred in fast zones, red means stop twenty feet back; left yields to right when you arrive together; give a bike three feet; stay five hundred feet behind a fire truck on a run.
Glossary: Move Over Law means the rule to shift a lane away from, or slow down for, stopped emergency and service vehicles showing lights; uncontrolled T intersection means a T junction with no sign or signal controlling it; ramp meter means a signal on a freeway entrance ramp where you stop while it shows red; gross misdemeanor means the more serious charge the manual applies to a repeat pedestrian or school patrol violation within a year; electric-assist bicycle means a bicycle with an electric motor that helps with pedaling.

corpus_stability.reason: The Minnesota Driver’s Manual prints a single edition line (June 2026) on its front cover and opens with a New laws and information chapter that collects recent changes in one place, with no sign of more than one rewrite per year in the selected pages.
